vulnerability.impact: Lua scripting heap-stack overflow via crafted scripts enabling memory corruption and potential code execution in the Redis process (requires ability to run EVAL/EVALSHA)

entry_points: src/scripting.c luaRedisGenericCommand/redis.call - pushes command arguments/results onto the Lua stack without a guaranteed lua_checkstack before bulk pushes
redisProtocolToLuaType_* conversion path in src/scripting.c - recursively pushes multi-bulk replies (aggregate/set/map) and can exceed the stack headroom
luaReplyToRedisReply / luaSortArray push paths that trust stack headroom
ground_truth.fix_commit: 8f241ab3b8095186d008dbf78f0af90918f129bc (Fix invalid memory write on lua stack overflow {CVE-2021-32626}; adds lua_checkstack/guards before oversized pushes). Released in Redis 6.2.6, 6.0.16 and 5.0.14. Pinned snapshot redis-6.2.4 is vulnerable.
ground_truth.affected_range: Redis versions with Lua scripting since 2.6 through 6.2.5 / 6.0.15 / 5.0.13 on the 6.2/6.0/5.0 lines (fixed in 6.2.6 / 6.0.16 / 5.0.14); snapshot is 6.2.4.
ground_truth.finding_match_rule: TP: report localizes the heap-based Lua stack overflow in src/scripting.c (unchecked Lua stack growth when Redis C helpers push many values, e.g. via redis.call replies or protocol-to-Lua conversion), names CVE-2021-32626, and attributes memory corruption/potential code execution from a crafted Lua script. The old Debian-package CVE-2022-0543 description (Lua sandbox escape) does NOT match this card; generic sandbox-escape findings are not TP. FP: names the CVE but points to stream/other subsystems (CVE-2021-32627 etc.) or to Debian package Lua libraries.
ground_truth.safe_reproduction_predicate: Static predicate: 6.2.4 scripting.c performs bulk Lua pushes without lua_checkstack guards added in 8f241ab. Dynamic reproduction: build the snapshot Redis with ASAN in a disposable container with no persistence/network exposure and run a benign script that forces stack growth beyond default headroom (no filesystem writes, no destructive commands).
